goal:
A reviewer asked me to double-check a value from the 2025 paper by Sørlie and colleagues on lattice relaxation in Letters in Mesoscale Ecology (http://letters-in-mesoscale-ecology.example/articles/23c2d0-a-stochastic-model-of-lattice-relaxation).
What mean annual runoff does Table 2 report for station M-09? Please give the value with its unit and tell me which source you used.

resources.title: A Stochastic Model of Lattice Relaxation
resources.version_label: Version of Record, Letters in Mesoscale Ecology (2025)

paragraphs: We study lattice relaxation across five monitoring stations using a mixed-effects model.
Authors: Elif Sørlie, Ximena Sandoval, Vera Hargreave. Published in Letters in Mesoscale Ecology, 2025.
Table 2 reports the mean annual runoff for each station.
body.table_caption: Table 2: Mean annual runoff by station

sections: Abstract

We report mean annual runoff measurements from five monitoring stations collected between 2023 and 2025. A pilot survey in 2020 had put the regional mean annual runoff at 174.7 mm; we find marked differences between upland and coastal sites.
1. Introduction
Earlier studies of lattice relaxation relied on single-site records [1, 2]. A multi-site campaign makes it possible to separate local effects from regional trends [3].
2. Methods

Station metadata are listed in Table 1. Measurements follow the protocol of [3]. Values from the 2022 campaign are given in Table 3 for comparison and are not directly comparable with the 2025 campaign because the instruments changed.
3. Results
Table 2 reports the mean annual runoff for each station in the 2025 campaign. The largest change relative to 2022 was observed at station R-31.
4. Discussion
The spread between stations exceeds the measurement uncertainty, which suggests that site conditions dominate. Longer records are needed to confirm the trend.
References
[1] Bianchi et al. (2019). [2] Kowalczyk and Oyelaran (2021). [3] Haldane et al. (2022).
